This appeal coming on for hearing this day, the court pa  following:
 ORDER This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is directed against the order dated 02.07.2009 passed by the First Additional Session Judge of Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior, (for short Tribunal) in Claim Case No.94/2007.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:

1

While the claimant was standing on right side, he was hit by offending vehicle / mini bus bearing No.MP07-G-1787, as a result, the appellant suffered injuries in left leg, pelvic bone and in private part.

Evidence is led as regards factum of the accident and also injuries suffered and issue arose as to whether the Insurance Company may be saddled with the liability of payment of compensation, if the driver of offending vehicle held driving license to drive light motor vehicle.
Admittedly, the Insurance Company did not lead any evidence that the weight of the offending vehicle in question was more than 7500 kg, so that the same can be treated to be a commercial vehicle.
The owner had remained ex-parte.
The present appellant - claimant has not led evidence as regards weight of the vehicle.

Under such circumstance, the Insurance Company treated the vehicle to be commercial vehicle and held that for want of endorsement in the license of driver for light motor vehicle authorizing him to drive commercial vehicle, the Insurance Company is not liable and entire liability for payment of compensation is shifted on the owner.
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation amount of Rs.43,840/-.
Mr. Haswani, counsel for the appellant - claimant submits that firstly the finding of the Tribunal in para - 16 is perverse and liable to be interfered.
Secondly, the amount of compensation awarded is on the lower side.

Learned counsel as regards first contention, submits that even if the driver had the license to drive light motor vehicle and was found driving commercial vehicle, the liability shall be that of Insurance Company to pay compensation as per the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., 2017 ACJ 2011.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., 2017 ACJ 2011
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, Insurance Company could not have been held liable for the same.
As regards second contention, it is submitted that the appellant was hospitalized for one month in Birla Hospital and documents in that regard have been produced before the trial Court.
Though the Tribunal has not considered those documents.
Hence, prays for enhancement of compensation.
Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that award passed by the Tribunal is legal and proper.
Hence, no exception thereto can be taken either on contention No.1 or contention No.2.

However, learned counsel for the Insurance Company does not dispute the legal position that even if the driver held license to drive light motor vehicle and if he was driving a mini bus, the liability may be that of the owner but the Insurance Company should have been directed to pay the amount and recover the same from the owner.
He relies upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pappu and others Vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and another, 2018 (1) T.A.C. 360 (SC).

entities.text: Pappu and others Vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and another, 2018 (1) T.A.C. 360 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, there is no appeal filed by the Insurance Company.
Indeed there is no evidence that the offending vehicle was weighing more than 7500 kg, though the vehicle is said to be a mini bus.

Under such circumstances, the judgment cited by the counsel for the appellant is found to be distinguishable on facts and is of no assistance but even if the driver holding the license for light motor vehicle and was driving commercial vehicle as found by the Tribunal, in all fairness the Tribunal ought to have ordered for pay and recover.
That has not been done.

Abhishek vs Kailash on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196773599/
2
Therefore, the impugned award deserves to be modified in that behalf.
Secondly, in the obtaining facts and circumstances, the amount of compensation i.e. Rs.43,000/- is enhanced to a lumsum amount of Rs.1,00,000/-.

Consequently, the appeal is allowed in part with a direction that Insurance Company shall pay the amount of Rs.1,00,000/- (if Rs.43,000/- is not paid) to the appellant within six weeks with right to recover the same from the owner.
Interest @ 6 % shall be payable on the entire amount of compensation from the date of application till the date of payment.

(ROHIT ARYA) JUDGE bj/-
